data.title: Transliteration Scheme Inconsistent with the Claimed Source Language
data.summary:
Foreign names and places in campaign content are romanised using a scheme specific to
one source language's transliteration standard, revealing the production team's actual
working language even though the published output is in a different one entirely.
data.description:
Every language that writes in the Latin alphabet has its own standardised convention for
rendering names from a non-Latin script, and the conventions disagree with each other in
specific, recognisable ways — a Cyrillic name rendered with "kh" and "-iy" follows
Russian romanisation; the same name rendered with "kh" and "-y" without the glide follows
a different standard. A production team defaults to whichever convention it already
knows, not the one the claimed output language's house style would use, and that default
survives translation of everything around it.

The tell is not reliable from a single name: legitimate outlets inconsistently inherit a
transliteration from newswire copy, which can look similar to this pattern without being
related to it at all. It becomes diagnostic when the same scheme is applied consistently,
across multiple names, in content that is not supposed to share a production chain with
anything using that scheme.
data.recommendation:
* Table every transliterated proper noun across the corpus and the romanisation scheme
  each follows; a single instance is coincidence, a consistent scheme across unrelated
  pieces is a production-language tell.
* Compare against the standard romanisation conventions of each candidate source language
  before naming one; several schemes overlap for common letter combinations and a weak
  match should stay a hypothesis.
* Rule out wire-copy reuse — legitimate outlets inconsistently inherit a transliteration
  from a newswire, producing a similar-looking but unrelated pattern.
* Weigh the finding alongside the corpus's other attribution indicators rather than
  naming a source language from transliteration alone.
data.short_recommendation: Table the transliteration scheme used for every proper noun and rule out wire-copy reuse before naming a source language.
